extracted.intended_audience: agency program managers, legal/compliance staff, and accessibility coordinators responsible for implementing Section 504 at the National Commission for Employment Policy (or similar federal agencies)
extracted.subtask_description: Implementing and administering nondiscrimination on the basis of handicap (Section 504) for programs and activities conducted by a federal agency, including accessibility, communications, complaint processing, and related definitions and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auxiliary aids (definition and examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Auxiliary aids means services or devices that enable persons with impaired sensory, manual, or speaking skills to have an equal opportunity to participate in, and enjoy the benefits of, programs or activities conducted by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: for impaired vision — readers, brailled materials, audio recordings, telecommunications devices; for impaired hearing — telephone handset amplifiers, telephones compatible with hearing aids, telecommunication devices for deaf persons (TDD's), interpreters, notetakers, written materials. Use this definition when determining what aids may be necessary to ensure equal opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete complaint (required elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete complaint means a written statement that contains the complainant’s name and address and describes the agency’s alleged discriminatory action in sufficient detail to inform the agency of the nature and date of the alleged violation of section 504; it shall be signed by the complainant or by someone authorized to do so on his or her behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaints filed on behalf of classes or third parties shall describe or identify (by name, if possible) the alleged victims of discrimination. Use this as the threshold for accepting and processing complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facility (scope of term)
rubrics_metrics.description: Facility means all or any portion of buildings, equipment, structures, roads, walks, parking lots, rolling stock or other conveyances, or other real or personal property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply this broad definition when assessing program accessibility and when notifying Architectural and Transportation Barriers Compliance Board for alleged facility barriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handicapped person (definition and subparts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Handicapped person means any person who has a physical or mental impairment that substantially limits one or more major life activities, has a record of such an impairment, or is regarded as having such an impairment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes (1) physiological disorders/conditions and mental or psychological disorders (lists examples such as cerebral palsy, epilepsy, cancer, heart disease, diabetes, mental retardation, drug addiction and alcoholism); (2) major life activities (caring for oneself, performing manual tasks, walking, seeing, hearing, speaking, breathing, learning, working); (3) 'has a record of' (history or misclassification); (4) 'is regarded as' (treated by the agency as having an impairment). Use these criteria when determining who is protected under the part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified handicapped person (context-specific definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualified handicapped person means, depending on context: (1) for preschool/elementary/secondary education, a handicapped person who is a member of a class otherwise entitled to receive education services; (2) for programs requiring services/levels of accomplishment, a handicapped person who meets essential eligibility requirements and can achieve program purpose without modifications that would cause fundamental alteration; (3) for other programs, a handicapped person who meets essential eligibility requirements; (4) for employment, definition in 29 CFR 1613.702(f) applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this multi-part definition to determine program eligibility and whether modifications are required or would fundamentally alter the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial impairment (historic preservation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantial impairment means a significant loss of the integrity of finished materials, design quality, or special character resulting from a permanent alteration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply when evaluating whether alterations to historic properties would be allowed under the historic-preservation exception to accessibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-evaluation requirement and recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall evaluate its current policies and practices that do not or may not meet the requirements of this part and, to the extent modification is required, proceed to make necessary modifications (deadline cited for August 24, 1987).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide opportunity for interested persons (including handicapped persons and organizations) to participate by submitting oral and written comments. Maintain on file and make available for public inspection for three years: (1) a description of areas examined and any problems identified; and (2) a description of any modifications made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirement (informing stakeholders)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall make available to employees, applicants, participants, beneficiaries, and other interested persons information regarding the provisions of this part and its applicability to the programs or activities conducted by the agency, and make such information available in such manner as the head of the agency finds necessary to apprise such persons of the protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor dissemination methods to reach the relevant populations and ensure accessibility of the information.

rubrics_metrics.name: General prohibitions against discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: No qualified handicapped person shall, on the basis of handicap, be excluded from participation in, denied the benefits of, or otherwise be subjected to discrimination under any program or activity conducted by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific prohibitions include: (i) denying opportunity to participate or benefit; (ii) affording unequal opportunity; (iii) providing aids, benefits, or services that are not as effective; (iv) providing different or separate aids unless necessary to provide equally effective benefits; (v) denying opportunity to participate as member of planning or advisory boards; (vi) otherwise limiting enjoyment of rights, privileges, advantages, or opportunities. Also prohibits use of criteria or administrative methods with purpose/effect of discrimination, discriminatory site/location selections, discriminatory procurement contractor selection criteria, and discriminatory administration of licensing/certification programs (with noted limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-segregation / participation in non-separate programs
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may not deny a qualified handicapped person the opportunity to participate in programs or activities that are not separate or different, despite the existence of permissibly separate or different programs or activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor inclusion in mainstream programs unless a permissible separate program is required and provides equivalent benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited administrative criteria and site-selection effects
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may not utilize criteria or methods of administration the purpose or effect of which would subject qualified handicapped persons to discrimination or defeat/substantially impair accomplishment of program objectives; nor may the agency, in determining site or location of a facility, make selections the purpose or effect of which would exclude handicapped persons or impair program objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess administrative criteria and site/location decisions for discriminatory purpose or effect before adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most integrated setting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall administer programs and activities in the most integrated setting appropriate to the needs of qualified handicapped persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When choosing among methods to meet accessibility, give priority to approaches offering programs in the most integrated setting appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment nondiscrimination and applicability of section 501 procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: No qualified handicapped person shall, on the basis of handicap, be subjected to discrimination in employment under any program or activity conducted by the agency; the definitions, requirements, and procedures of section 501 (29 U.S.C. 791) and EEOC regulations at 29 CFR part 1613 apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handle employment-related complaints / procedures in accordance with EEOC-established processes; consult 29 CFR part 1613 for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program accessibility — general rule for existing facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall operate each program or activity so that the program or activity, when viewed in its entirety, is readily accessible to and usable by handicapped persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This does not require making each existing facility accessible; exceptions include historic preservation concerns and actions that would result in fundamental alteration or undue financial/administrative burdens (agency bears burden of proof and must provide written statement of reasons). If structural changes would cause such burdens/alteration, agency must take other actions that do not cause them but still ensure handicapped persons receive program benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods to achieve program accessibility (existing facilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may comply through redesign of equipment, reassignment of services to accessible buildings, assignment of aides to beneficiaries, home visits, delivery of services at alternate accessible sites, alteration of existing facilities and construction of new facilities, use of accessible rolling stock, or any other methods that result in making its programs or activities readily accessible and usable by handicapped persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structural changes are not required where other methods are effective. In choosing methods, give priority to those that offer programs in the most integrated setting appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historic preservation programs — special methods and priority
rubrics_metrics.description: In historic preservation programs, give priority to methods that provide physical access to handicapped persons; where physical alteration is not required due to historic-preservation or undue-burden exceptions, alternative methods include audio-visual materials to depict inaccessible portions, assigning persons to guide handicapped persons through portions that cannot be made accessible, or adopting other innovative methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance preservation of historic features against accessibility; document reasons for not undertaking physical alterations when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time period for compliance (deadlines)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall comply with obligations under § 500.150 by October 21, 1986, except that structural changes in facilities shall be made by August 22, 1989; in any event, compliance must be as expeditiously as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meet program-wide accessibility by the stated dates and prioritize prompt action for structural changes where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition plan requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If structural changes will be undertaken to achieve program accessibility, the agency shall develop a transition plan (deadline Feb 23, 1987) setting forth steps necessary to complete such changes and provide opportunity for interested persons (including handicapped persons/organizations) to participate by submitting comments; the plan must be available for public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan must, at a minimum: (1) identify physical obstacles in the agency’s facilities that limit accessibility; (2) describe in detail methods to make facilities accessible; (3) specify schedule for steps necessary to achieve compliance and, if longer than one year, identify steps for each year; (4) indicate official responsible for implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program accessibility — new construction and alterations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each building or part of a building constructed or altered by, on behalf of, or for the use of the agency shall be designed, constructed, or altered so as to be readily accessible to and usable by handicapped persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definitions, requirements, and standards of the Architectural Barriers Act (42 U.S.C. 4151–4157) and implementing regulations (41 CFR 101–19.600 to 101–19.607) apply to buildings covered by this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications — effective communication and auxiliary aids obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall take appropriate steps to ensure effective communication with applicants, participants, personnel of other Federal entities, and members of the public, including furnishing appropriate auxiliary aids where necessary to afford an equal opportunity to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In determining type of auxiliary aid, give primary consideration to requests of the handicapped person. Agency need not provide individually prescribed devices, readers for personal use or study, or other personal devices. Telephone communications must use TDDs or equally effective systems. Ensure persons with impaired vision or hearing can obtain information about accessible services and facilities; provide signage at primary entrances to inaccessible facilities directing users to information locations; use the international symbol for accessibility at primary entrance of accessible facilities. Exceptions for fundamental alteration/undue burdens apply (agency bears burden and must provide written statement) — if exception applies, agency must take any other action that would not result in such burdens but would, to the maximum extent possible, ensure handicapped persons receive program benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of compliance procedures (scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in paragraph (b), § 500.170 applies to all allegations of discrimination on the basis of handicap in programs or activities conducted by the agency. Employment-related allegations are processed according to EEOC procedures under 29 CFR part 1613 pursuant to section 501.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know which complaint channels apply depending on subject matter (general program complaints vs employment complaints).

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint filing timeframe and acceptance (180 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: All complete complaints for which the agency has jurisdiction must be filed within 180 days of the alleged act of discrimination; the agency may extend this time period for good cause. The agency shall accept and investigate all complete complaints for which it has jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 180-day filing limit as the standard deadline; consider extensions only for good cause and document any extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral and notice when no jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: If the agency receives a complaint over which it does not have jurisdiction, it shall promptly notify the complainant and shall make reasonable efforts to refer the complaint to the appropriate government entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promptly inform complainants and assist in referral to ensure complaints are addressed by the proper authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify Architectural and Transportation Barriers Compliance Board
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall notify the Architectural and Transportation Barriers Compliance Board upon receipt of any complaint alleging that a building or facility subject to the Architectural Barriers Act or section 502 of the Rehabilitation Act is not readily accessible to and usable by handicapped persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure required notifications are made when complaints implicate Architectural Barriers Act jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation results letter contents and deadline (180 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 180 days of receipt of a complete complaint for which it has jurisdiction, the agency shall notify the complainant of the results of the investigation in a letter containing: (1) findings of fact and conclusions of law; (2) a description of a remedy for each violation found; and (3) a notice of the right to appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear, timely (180-day) written decision that includes factual and legal bases, remedies for each violation, and appeal rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals filing timeframe (90 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals of the findings of fact and conclusions of law or remedies must be filed by the complainant within 90 days of receipt from the agency of the letter required by § 500.170(g). The agency may extend this time for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 90 days as standard appeal filing window; document and justify any extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals processing and decision deadlines (head of agency responsibilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Timely appeals shall be accepted and processed by the head of the agency. The head of the agency shall notify the complainant of the results of the appeal within 60 days of the receipt of the request; if additional information is needed from the complainant, the head has 60 days from receipt of that information to make a determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with 60-day decision timeline for appeals, and allow one additional 60-day window if more information is requested; document any delays and reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time limits with Assistant Attorney General permission
rubrics_metrics.description: The time limits cited in paragraphs (g) and (j) (investigation results and appeal decision deadlines) may be extended with the permission of the Assistant Attorney General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain and document Assistant Attorney General permission prior to extending deadlines under § 500.170(g) and (j).

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of investigative authority (limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may delegate its authority for conducting complaint investigations to other Federal agencies, except that the authority for making the final determination may not be delegated to another agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure any delegation arrangement preserves the agency's ultimate responsibility to make final determinations and is documented.
